clues.title: Road line: Roadlines
text: Roads in Oman use yellow outer and white middle lines.
**NOTE:** This is also common in the UAE, Israel, Jordan, as well as occasionally found in Qatar.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Fasad Dunes
text: A road going through large orange-pink sand dunes can be found north of Fasad.
NOTE: The same dunes can be seen in the distance close to the northern part of the Yemen border.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Ubar Fields
text: Around the town of Ubar, you can find patches of green agricultural land surrounded by desert.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Landscape: Masirah Island
text: Masirah Island features a dry and slightly hilly landscape, typically with somewhat grey soil and with brown shrubs visible. Road 51, which circulates the island, usually only has a white centre road line, which can help in recognising it. The front camera on the island is slightly smudged.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Bidiyah Shrubby Desert
text: Sandy desert with light coloured green and yellow shrubs can be found in northeastern Oman, mainly south and west of Bidiyah.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Landscape: Salalah Hills
text: Close to the southern coast, especially around Salalah, you will find a rolling hills landscape. The area commonly features rocky ground, bushes and small trees as well as some fairly green valleys.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Landscape: Eastern Mountain Range
text: Northern Oman features a dry mountainous landscape similar to eastern UAE. The south coast of Oman also rarely features some similar mountains.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Curbs
text: Black-and-yellow curbs are common in Oman.
The UAE also commonly uses similar curbs.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Coverage: Car
text: All the coverage in Oman was taken with a white pickup truck, meaning you will either see most of the car or a large front blur.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Plate: License Plates
text: Licence plates on private vehicles are generally yellow, while commercial vehicles have red plates.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Direction sign: Striped Signposts
text: Many signposts in Oman have black-and-white stripes.
Within the Middle East, striped signposts are only found in Oman and the UAE.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Landscape: Landscape
text: Most of Oman features a desert landscape with little vegetation.
While the middle and southern half is mostly flat, the north coast features dry mountains similar to those found in the UAE.
The southern coast also has mountains, though less dry.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

This is also common in the UAE, Israel, Jordan, as well as occasionally found in Qatar.

clues.title: Chevron: Chevrons
text: Oman uses black-and-yellow chevrons that have an unusually large number of arrows.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: High Voltage Pylons
text: High voltage pylons painted with a red and white pattern are common in Oman.
Within the Middle East, red and white painted pylons can also less commonly be found in Qatar.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Garbage Bins
text: The vast majority of garbage bins in Oman are either black and made of plastic or metallic and grey, with a three-leaf logo and the text ‘be’ah’ below it.
Garbage bins in the UAE will occasionally have the text “bee’ah”, with two E’s.
The bins are often more colourful too.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Architecture: Light-Colored Stone
text: Buildings in Oman are typically made of light-coloured stone.
The houses are ‘blocky’ but still quite ornate, and they are usually surrounded by a matching fence, which often has an even more ornate gate.
Buildings in the UAE are often very similar.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)
